_comment: THE ATTESTATION REGISTRY. One home for how much evidence stands behind each law (D-039,
D-040). Checked by check_attestation() in tools/check-corpus.py against the `law`
vocabulary in tools/vocabularies.json.
WHY THIS FILE IS LIVING AND provenance/lineage.md IS NOT. The tally in lineage.md is a
FROZEN record of the 2026-07-20 extraction (L-13). It is annotated by addendum, never
edited -- so it cannot carry L-18, and it cannot carry a correction. That is correct
behaviour for a frozen record and useless as a live source of truth, which is why the two
coexist: lineage.md is the evidence this file was derived from, and this file is what the
gate reads. This is the frozen/living split, not a second home for one fact.
GRADE IS ORTHOGONAL TO BINDING. Every law binds at every tier whatever its grade. The
grade governs how readily the rule is amended when a project pushes back on it, and
whether it owes a sunset. See doctrine/01-laws.md.
ASTRONOMER CANNOT ATTEST ITS OWN LAWS. This corpus has twice broken L-14 and built a gate
for it (AMENDS D-015, D-019), and those incidents do NOT raise L-14 to settled. The four
source projects were independent of each other and of a framework that did not yet exist;
the framework applying its own rule to itself is not a fifth independent arrival, it is
the same claim looking in a mirror. D-007 says Astronomer governs itself. It does not say
Astronomer corroborates itself.
WHAT THIS CANNOT CATCH. Whether a listed source project ACTUALLY arrived at the rule
independently. That judgement was made once, at extraction, by a reader who could see all
four corpora, and it is not re-derivable from here. A wrongly-credited source would pass
this gate silently, and the only instrument that would catch it is re-reading the sources.
review_event: The next installation of Astronomer into a project. An EVENT, not a date -- dates get missed, and an install is the only moment at which a second project is actually available to attest anything. rituals/starting-a-project.md carries the step.
derived_from: provenance/lineage.md tally (frozen 2026-07-20), cross-checked against the per-law `Attested` lines in doctrine/01-laws.md. The two agreed on all seventeen seeded laws, independently. L-18 comes from the 2026-07-26T23:07Z addendum.

laws.title: Supersede by name
laws.would_attest: A third project that independently requires a superseding decision to NAME what it replaces, rather than resolving two live rules by recency.

laws.title: Scope is mandatory
laws.would_attest: A third project that independently makes the conditions of a claim a REQUIRED field rather than a convention, and routes unscoped claims to scrutiny.

laws.title: Co-occurrence is not shared cause
laws.would_attest: A third project that independently refuses to group findings by co-occurrence until a shared mechanism is cited at a location.

laws.title: No changes during observation
laws.would_attest: A third project that independently forbids intervention inside an observation window, including one-line obvious fixes.

laws.title: Validate small first
laws.would_attest: A third project that independently gates an expensive run on a sample small enough to check by hand.

laws.title: One variable at a time
laws.would_attest: A third project that independently attributes a wrong result to two changes landing together, or designs an experiment down to a single differing variable.

laws.title: Measure your own baseline
laws.would_attest: A second project that independently requires its own baseline measurement rather than a quoted figure. FR's read-only progress dashboard and DD's measured-only-never-inferred invariant were judged at seeding to be the same instinct arriving by a different route and NOT to count. That judgement is the first thing a second look should revisit -- it is the only grade in this registry resting on a close call rather than an absence.

laws.title: Verify at the right altitude
laws.would_attest: A third project that independently records a proxy measurement which could not have failed in the way that mattered, or publishes what its own tooling cannot measure.

laws.title: Vocabulary has one home
laws.would_attest: A third project that independently gives each shared term one enforced home and renders every consumer from it. NOTE: this corpus supplies two negative instances of its own (AMENDS D-015, D-019) and they do NOT count -- see the comment above on why Astronomer cannot attest itself.

laws.title: Name the non-delegable
laws.would_attest: A third project that independently names its human-only work in writing before starting, and halts there rather than producing a plausible substitute.

laws.title: Gate, do not re-fix
laws.would_attest: A third project that independently converts a recurring defect into a mechanism instead of fixing its next instance.

laws.title: An instrument declares its limits
laws.would_attest: A second project that independently requires an instrument -- tool, collaborator, or environment -- to declare what it cannot do before work depends on it. The nearest available signal would be a project adopting a capability inventory or an operator profile WITHOUT being instructed to, which is weaker than an independent arrival and should be recorded as such rather than counted.
